title: Terraform module: EKS control plane sequence validator & upgrade safety hook
text:
Terraform module: EKS control plane sequence validator & upgrade safety hook

description:
Add a lightweight Terraform module and associated runtime hooks that validate upgrade sequencing and pre/post health checks for Redwood Private EKS control plane provisioning. The module (infra/terraform/modules/eks/sequence-validator) will run preflight validations, emit a deterministic upgrade plan token, and install optional probes that validate API-server/cert rotation timing, control-plane endpoint stability, and KMS/S3 state integrity before terraform apply proceeds. Goal: reduce failed control plane upgrades and provide a reproducible, auditable safety gate for both self-serve Private installs and automated fleet upgrades.

acceptance_criteria:
New terraform module path created: infra/terraform/modules/eks/sequence-validator
Preflight checks run in 'terraform plan' CI step and fail fast with actionable message when gating conditions not met
Upgrade token and sequence file written to state bucket with TTL and digital signature (kms key ARN recorded)
Automated canary cluster workflow consumes sequence token and either proceeds or triggers rollback policy
Observability: Grafana dashboard shows validator metrics (validator_pass_total, validator_failures, last_sequence_token)
Documentation: Confluence runbook + PRD updated and linked from module README

implementation_notes:
Module will be implemented as a thin wrapper around existing controlplane module; pure Terraform where possible with local-exec for small verification tasks
Preflight checks include: S3 state lock availability, KMS decrypt/encrypt roundtrip, control plane API health endpoint (HEAD /healthz with sigverify), certificate expiry windows, existing nodegroup drain-safe windows
Sequence token: HMAC-signed JSON payload with cluster_id, target_version, ordered_steps; stored in s3://redwood-priv-state/<cluster>/sequences/<token>.json
If Terraform Cloud/remote backend used, token writing will use role-assumed short-lived credentials; otherwise use module parameter for state bucket ARN
A small DaemonSet (python + curl) will be optional for in-cluster post-upgrade checks; annotated as opt-in for customers who want intra-cluster validation
RBAC and KMS permissions must be documented; will add new IAM role for verifier-runner with least privilege to read state, write sequence token, and call kms:Encrypt/Decrypt
We will prefer idempotent checks so re-running the validator is safe. Avoid stateful side effects except for S3 token write which is atomic and TTL-based

rollout_plan:
1) Merge module with feature flag off. Add unit/acceptance tests in infra repo.
2) Run on internal dogfood clusters (priv-dogfood-01, -02) with manual gate; collect metrics for 2 weeks
3) Enable in automated canary pipeline for low-risk clusters (alpha tier) with auto-notify to infra-oncall on failures
4) Gradually increase to all Dedicated/Private clusters after 4 successful canaries
5) Default enable for new clusters created after release date; existing clusters opt-in via apply to change module config

testing:
Unit: terraform validate + kitchen-terraform tests for happy/failure preflight scenarios
Integration: run module against ephemeral EKS control plane (ci-eks-seq-*) and simulate KMS and S3 failures
Chaos test: induce certificate expiry and API-server latency during canary to ensure validator blocks faulty upgrades
End-to-end: full upgrade run using sequence token passing through pipeline + canary verification + rollback trigger
Monitoring test: validate metrics exported to prometheus and alerting thresholds (e.g., >3 failures in 1h triggers P0)

comments:
2026-02-21 — Asha Nair: Initial spike complete. Prototype writes token to test S3 bucket and validates KMS roundtrip. Saved proof-of-concept in infra/experiments/seq-val.
2026-02-26 — Mateo Ortega: Reworked token schema to include ordered step IDs and hash of terraform plan. This lets canary agents assert plan immutability before applying.
2026-03-02 — Infra Eng Review (L. Chen): Suggested moving certificate checks earlier in sequence; added explicit check for 'apiserver cert rotation window' to avoid mid-upgrade rotation races.
2026-03-05 — Security (R. Patel): Reviewed IAM scope. Requested explicit kms:GenerateDataKey permission and separate role for verifier-runner. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-08 — Mateo Ortega: Opened WIP PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2486. CI currently failing on provider version pin (aws provider 5.x -> 6.x compatibility). Pending fix in ENG-531413.
2026-03-12 — Asha Nair: Added acceptance criteria for observability. Implemented prometheus metric exposition in prototype; pushing metrics to dogfood cluster for validation.
